quest.title: The Magician's Secret
quest.description: Lyney and you agreed to meet outside Hotel Debord. Go meet him at the appointed time.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x750, Mora x44000, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x10

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Over here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Lynette's not joining us today?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: I've had her follow Jemma and see if we can make any inroads with her. They should be at a cafe right now.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Still... I don't think that Jemma's likely to open up to us. *sigh* So we need a contingency plan.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Today, we'll be looking into a guy named Lorenzo, Cesar's former pupil and assistant.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: When Cesar passed away, all the stolen goods discovered in his home were confiscated and returned to their rightful owners. But Lorenzo was the only one privy to all his magic secrets, and he inherited his craft.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Before long, Lorenzo was the next big magician in town, his fame surpassing even that of his master, and it made him very wealthy. He's since left the magic scene though, and these days, he's a wealthy businessman with his fingers in a lot of different pies.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: I had to pull a lot of strings, but I managed to get him to agree to a couple of drinks with me. Be warned, though — I hear he's got a hair-trigger temper. We'd best be careful.

talks.objective: Talk to Lorenzo at the hotel

dialogues.speaker: Lorenzo
dialogues.text: You neglected to mention that you were bringing two other people with you.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: My apologies, these two are my assistants. When they heard that I was meeting with the former magic maestro himself, they begged and pleaded with me to bring them along... Um, and if it's no trouble, a couple of autographs would really make their day...

dialogues.speaker: Lorenzo
dialogues.text: Hmph. Forget the pleasantries. Just sit.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Get a load of this guy... "Forget the pleasantries," he says, but he looks pretty happy about Lyney stroking his ego...

dialogues.speaker: Lorenzo
dialogues.text: I only agreed to meet since we're both magicians. Do me a favor and cut to the chase — I have more important things to do than drinking.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Much obliged, Sir. As it happens, the matter I want to address is also related to magic.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Yesterday morning, a warning letter from The Phantom Weasel appeared on the entrance to the opera house. He claims to be planning something for the same evening that I'm scheduled to do a magic show there. As such, I believe that I may well be his target.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: I have to get to the bottom of this to ensure that my show can go ahead as planned. Naturally, any investigation into The Weasel starts with a few questions about Cesar, who—

dialogues.speaker: Lorenzo
dialogues.text: What is there to investigate?

dialogues.speaker: Lorenzo
dialogues.text: Cesar was The Weasel, and he's been dead for ten years. So what if some sick creep thought it'd be funny to write a warning letter? It changes nothing! Are you trying to tell me you actually bought it?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Please, Sir, no need to get so worked up. I do concede that a copycat is but one possibility...

dialogues.speaker: Lorenzo
dialogues.text: Possibility? It's a fact, Lyney. Look, my patience is limited, so listen carefully while I'm still willing to put up with you.

dialogues.speaker: Lorenzo
dialogues.text: The Weasel is dead, period. Everyone knows that. So do yourself a favor, and quit this investigation — it'll lead you nowhere. Look, if this affects your magic show in any way, I will personally compensate you for any losses.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Oh... Sir, I'm... honored, really, but this isn't about finances for me.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: My pride as a magician is what's at stake here, Lorenzo. Copycat or not, this person has thrown me the gauntlet — and I must meet their challenge head-on.

dialogues.speaker: Lorenzo
dialogues.text: Your pride? Hah! Don't mince words with me, boy. Just tell me, what exactly are you seeking to do?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: I want to find out The Phantom Weasel's true identity. I have to know for myself what really happened ten years ago.

dialogues.speaker: Lorenzo
dialogues.text: What would that accomplish? And what do the events of ten years ago have to do with you, anyway? Look, you of all people should know that a magician never reveals their secrets — and in any case, dead men don't talk. So if you really care about your magician's pride, then you'll forget about Cesar and move on.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh-oh, this is getting awkward...
Lorenzo? Is that— It is you! I know that big... booming voice anywhere. What's up, my man? Wanna grab a drink with me?

dialogues.speaker: Lorenzo
dialogues.text: Another day. I'm busy.
Ah, come on, you can't be all business all the... time. You know what they say, live fast, die... young. You gotta learn how to kick back and relax once in a while.

dialogues.speaker: Lorenzo
dialogues.text: If I wanted your life advice, I'd ask for it. Now, get out of my face and go be drunk somewhere else.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Sorry, my good sir, I don't believe I've had the pleasure...

dialogues.speaker: Edmondo
dialogues.text: Oh, hey. I'm Edmondo. He and I are business pals, we've worked together a bunch of times.

dialogues.speaker: Edmondo
dialogues.text: This your first time meeting him? He's always like this — foul-mouthed and hard-nosed. Never heard a kind word outta this guy the whole time I've known him.

dialogues.speaker: Edmondo
dialogues.text: And he wonders why he can't get a girlfriend, despite being... what, pushing forty? Thirty-something, anyway — the point is, a lot older than when he first got rejected by the girl he was into... and is still into, from what I hear...

dialogues.speaker: Lorenzo
dialogues.text: Shut up, and get out of my face. Another word out of you, and you can forget about doing business with me ever again. Do I make myself clear?

dialogues.speaker: Edmondo
dialogues.text: Haha... Sorry, I may have had a liiiiittle too much to drink... Alright, I'm gonna leave. Don't work too hard.

dialogues.speaker: Lorenzo
dialogues.text: I think it's high time I made a move as well. If you really want to investigate this, Lyney, be my guest.

dialogues.speaker: Lorenzo
dialogues.text: But if nothing good comes of it, don't say I didn't warn you.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Well, that fell to pieces in a rather spectacular fashion... Any thoughts?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There's something strange about him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Totally. And what was all that about compensating you for your losses? Why would someone you've just met make an offer like that?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He's gotta be hiding something... And not like Jemma. She was little suspicious, but this guy's definitely covering something up.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: I think so too. We need to look into Lorenzo more closely.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: That guy Edmondo seems to know a thing or two about him. He only just left — let's see if we can catch up with him.

dialogues.speaker: Edmondo
dialogues.text: Ugh... *cough*...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: You okay there?

dialogues.speaker: Edmondo
dialogues.text: Uhh... Who are you?

dialogues.speaker: Edmondo
dialogues.text: Oh... You guys. Don't worry about me, I must've had one too many... Just need to ride it out.

dialogues.speaker: Edmondo
dialogues.text: I said waaay too much back there, didn't I? Nearly talked myself into complete financial ruin... Note to self: No more drunken chats when Lorenzo's around.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So he was serious about threatening to cut you off? Ugh, Paimon knew he was a bad egg!

dialogues.speaker: Edmondo
dialogues.text: Hey, hey, hey! Keep your voice down!

dialogues.speaker: Edmondo
dialogues.text: Don't go prying into Lorenzo's personal affairs... Bad things happen to people who ask too many questions or make an enemy out of him.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: What kind of bad things?

dialogues.speaker: Edmondo
dialogues.text: Don't even ask. I'm sorry, I'm gonna have to cut this conversation short. I'm not crossing that line again.

dialogues.speaker: Edmondo
dialogues.text: And take it from me: Trouble with Lorenzo is one thing you don't need in your life. You saw him flare up back there — I don't know what you said to him, but clearly it touched a nerve.

dialogues.speaker: Edmondo
dialogues.text: That's not a good sign. You're too young for this — don't get in over your head. I'm leaving.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And there he goes... What do we do now, Lyney?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Shhh. I think we're being watched. Someone was listening in to our whole conversation.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Don't say anything, and don't look back. Any altercation in the city will attract the Gardes... We'd better take this elsewhere.

talks.objective: Get out of the city and lure out the people tailing you

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: You've followed us a long way. Why don't you come out and introduce yourselves?

dialogues.speaker: "Smoothface" Paccino
dialogues.text: So you're Lyney? And where's your sister, ain't she with you today?

dialogues.speaker: "Smoothface" Paccino
dialogues.text: Save us the trouble and go fetch her for us. Let's not drag this out.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon doesn't like the tone of your voice, mister! Who sent you, huh?

dialogues.speaker: "Painter" De Niro
dialogues.text: Save your questions, missy. You ain't gonna need answers where you're goin', capiche?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: *sigh* Looks like we can't avoid this fight.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Now, I'm not the strongest fighter, so I hope you're ready to back me up.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't worry, we got this!

dialogues.speaker: "Smoothface" Paccino
dialogues.text: Curses! They're tougher than we thought...

dialogues.speaker: "Painter" De Niro
dialogues.text: Vision-wielders are always trouble! Intimidation ain't gonna work like it did on the lady...

dialogues.speaker: "Smoothface" Paccino
dialogues.text: C'mon! Let's scram!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, wise guys! We ain't through with you yet...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Grr, they got away! Did you catch what they said just before they left? Something about intimidating someone else?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds like they just wanted to rough us up as a scare-tactic... and they've already done it to someone else. But who?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Could it be Jemma?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're right! She was injured when we saw her yesterday, and she acted like she had something to hide...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Maybe she was too scared to tell us the truth because those guys had threatened her.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Hmm... Well if that's the case, she should be more willing to open up to us once she learns that those thugs won't be bothering her anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Let's head back to the cafe and see if we can get any information from her.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Jemma?

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: You again... What is it this time?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We just ran into the men who've been threatening you... And we gave 'em a taste of their own medicine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So you can relax now. We're here to protect you!

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: What? Why? ...I didn't tell you anything. Why would they come after you?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Hmm. Sounds like they're no strangers to you.

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: That's putting it mildly. I know them all too well... and I hate them with every fiber of my being.

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: It's been ten long years... And still, every time I try to look into Cesar's death, they show up and warn me not to "do anything stupid"...

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: ...How do I know I can trust you? Do you really think you can get to the bottom of it all? And... Why are you doing this?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: I'm afraid I can't reveal all the details just yet, but I can promise you this — I will expose The Phantom Weasel's true identity.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Because you see, this is a personal matter of the utmost importance. I give you my word. Trust me.

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: ...Okay. How can I help you?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: I've heard that Cesar used to have a magic workshop where he kept a lot of his personal effects. If possible, I'd like to take a look at them.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Do you know where it is?

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: The Fleuve Cendre. But the place was sealed up by the police after his death, and no one's been there since.

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: I also know that The Fleuve Cendre is dangerous territory — lots of hostile groups lurking around. If you're serious about going there... please be careful.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Understood. Lynette, you stay here and take care of Jemma. Don't let her come to harm.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Got it. But if I'm staying here, I'm ordering dessert...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: I mean... bon appetit, but stay sharp too. They're likely to come for you while I'm away.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Kay... Alright, power-saving mode off. I'll start taking this more seriously now.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: If Jemma gave us the right location, then the workshop should be right nearby... Huh, looks like these boxes are blocking the entrance. Let's shift them away first.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You help Lyney move the boxes aside. It looks like no one's been here in a long time...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: There we go! It should be just down here.

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: ...Lynette? Fancy meeting you here.

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: Can I get you something to drink?

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: No need.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: With me here, nothing will happen.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's weird. Have we reached the end already?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There's nothing here. Maybe this was a wasted trip...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Lyney, what're you looking at?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: This place seems a little too ordinary for a magician's workshop. There's a distinct lack of mystery.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: We've triggered quite a few devices on the way here. I'm starting to wonder whether Cesar built this whole place as one big, elaborate magic contraption.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: If so, then there must be more to this place than meets the eye. Maybe a hidden room somewhere.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Aha. If I just move this book, then hopefully... and, presto!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A secret passageway! How did you know?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: I'm a magician too. And apparently, great minds really do think alike.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Looks pretty big inside. Let's head in and take a look around.

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: Whatever you do... Please be careful.

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: If anything happens to you because you're investigating Cesar, I'll never be able to forgive myself...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why've you stopped, Lyney? Is there some device in that box?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Huh... It just looks familiar, somehow. Lemme check this out for a second while you guys go on ahead.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: If anyone makes a major discovery, let's rendezvous here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright. See ya in a bit!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Stop Reading

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Two magic geniuses with a "Father" and a mission, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds a lot like he was writing about Lyney and Lynette, don't you think?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So did they meet Cesar when they were kids? Let's go ask Lyney.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Lyney—

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Shh, hold that thought... As I expected, there's a lot of fishy things going on in this place.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Fishy? Uh-oh, what have you found?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: All in good time. Before we go over our new leads, I wanna tell you how a "high-altitude escape" is performed.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: First, the magician slots themselves into a magic box in full view of the audience. The box is then suspended high in the air, and a short while later, the base automatically opens.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: At this point, a dummy will fall out of the box, but it looks real enough to grab the audience's attention, and they start wailing and screaming...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Meanwhile, the real magician — who has by now blended into the crowd — waits for a good moment to make their appearance and put on a hysterical performance:

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: "Oh no! Is that me!? Did I just fall to my death!?"

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Very vivid description, Paimon can really picture it... and then what?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: The audience's gaze then turns to the magician, and by the time they realize what's happened, the dummy has vanished — as if everything that just happened was some sort of shared illusion.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Of course, that's just how I think the process should work, theoretically speaking.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Theoretically speaking? What do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: The inventor of this trick never performed it successfully. When the box opened... Cesar was the one who fell out, and not the dummy.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: He fell right to the ground from the highest point of the opera house... No one could hope to survive that fall — not without a Vision, at least.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: And no one else has ever attempted this trick since. My understanding of how it works is just based on what I could gather from his notes and the relevant gadgets here in his workshop.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So Cesar's famous high-altitude escape has never been done, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon was about to say how cool it would be to see it in person. But if it's that dangerous, it's probably for the best that no one else tries to do it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait a second, so if a dummy's supposed to drop out of the box, then where does the real magician go? How does he get out?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Glad you asked — that brings us to the secret of said box.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: This box right here is the one that Cesar constructed himself to use in the performance, and it's not as simple as it looks. Inside, there's a device that only the magician himself would know about.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Once the magician's inside, and the box is lifted up into the air, the audience's view of the box is fixed at a certain angle.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: From where they're standing, they have a clear view of the front, sides, and bottom, but the back and the top are now no longer visible.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: At this point, the magician presses a button inside the box, opening a secret door out of view.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: He then escapes through this trap door onto the opera house roof, waits for the dummy to fall and distract the audience, and quietly returns to ground level.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's way simpler than Paimon imagined. Even Paimon could probably do it!

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Haha, well, there's a little more to it than that, of course. The hardest part of this trick is controlling the audience's mood and reactions. That takes an exceptional degree of showmanship.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: There's the falling dummy, the miraculous reappearance, the pompous performing... Maybe the magician would even have themselves tied up before it begins to strengthen the impression that there's no escape.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Many days and nights of careful research and painstaking practice would have gone into this, all culminating in a performance just a few minutes long — but one that still manages to transform the shock and grief of a tragic accident to the joy and laughter of a mesmerizing magic trick.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Cesar was a highly accomplished magician... But unfortunately, even he didn't manage to pull it off.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... How did it go so wrong? You said you found some fishy stuff here — have you figured out what really happened?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: ...I can make a pretty good guess.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: I looked into the case files. The magic box Cesar was using at the time of his death had the secret button I mentioned positioned on the right-hand side. And sure enough, he always used his right hand as his dominant hand in public.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay... Nothing suspicious there...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: But here's the strange thing: Most of the devices in this workshop have the mechanism on the left-hand side, including this box right here. Which leads me to believe that Cesar was, in fact, left-handed.

choices.text: I'm not sure where you're going with this.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Because a magician can't afford to have their most basic habits stand out too much. People naturally focus their attention on the most important details of the task or situation at hand.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: But a magician needs to be able to redirect an audience's attention at will, so as to avoid arousing their suspicion.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: The essence of magic is getting people to believe a lie. If even the truth raises eyebrows, the falsehoods become all the more difficult to mask.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: And so, Cesar trained himself to use his right hand to align with his audience's expectations... Great magic always requires sacrifices.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: But in his most stressful and nerve-wracking moments, and when no one was watching, reflex would kick in and he'd use his left hand. That's why he set his gadgets with the mechanism on his left.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Maybe someone exploited that fact against him?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Exactly. I think that's likely what happened.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Cesar would have been under a lot of time pressure during the escape. He'd have had mere seconds to open the hidden compartment, retrieve the dummy, then open the secret door and make a swift escape.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: But I'm sure he was confident. He would have rehearsed countless times, to the point where it was second nature. He'd barely need to think about what he was doing, because muscle memory would guide him through.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: So he opened the compartment, took out the dummy, checked everything was in order, and then went to leave. With his left hand, he reached for the button, and suddenly his heart skipped a beat — it wasn't there.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Much like when you reach for your keys but find your pocket empty, his mind needed a moment to process what was going on.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Instinctively, his left hand would keep feeling around for the missing button, maybe for another second or two... until the bottom of the box gave way.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: With the stakes being as high as they were, just a two-second delay cost him everything. The authorities would find nothing suspicious, and conclude that his death was due to his own error.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: When in reality, someone switched the boxes... and they did it to murder him.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But how would they be able to make the switch without being noticed? That would be difficult to pull off, no?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: It would have to have been someone who knew that he was left-handed, and who could move his props around without arousing suspicion. Someone who was always by his side.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Isn't that right... Lorenzo?

response.speaker: Lorenzo
response.text: You just couldn't let sleeping dogs lie, could you?

response.speaker: Lorenzo
response.text: There's not a lot of people who'd go to all this trouble for some magician who died ten years ago. I didn't want to have to do this, you know... Silencing you the hard way just creates more problems for me to deal with.

response.speaker: Lorenzo
response.text: But I gave you your chance. I hoped you'd do what's good for you and back off, like the lady, but... you disappoint me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You mean Jemma? So YOU are the one who's been threatening her!

response.speaker: Lorenzo
response.text: Yes, although however stubborn she might be, she was never much of a liability. But you people... You never even knew him, but for some reason you just wouldn't drop it...

response.speaker: Lorenzo
response.text: Which is why you can't leave this place alive. Take them out. And make it quick.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmph, do your worst!!!

choices.text: Why would Cesar pretend to be right-handed?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: The placement of this device inside... Hmm, if I remember correctly...

talks.objective: Get the truth behind Cesar's death from Lorenzo

dialogues.speaker: Lorenzo
dialogues.text: *cough* ...Ugh, you kids are tougher than you look...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Had enough yet, Lorenzo? Your cronies can't help you now.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: I think it's high time you started talking, and what I'd really like to know is... Why did you murder Cesar?

dialogues.speaker: Lorenzo
dialogues.text: Ugh, if I had a Mora for every time you've said that man's name... Of course you idolize Cesar, everyone else did. But I was the real genius magician! Me!

dialogues.speaker: Lorenzo
dialogues.text: He was just an amateur who did cheap tricks for gullible children. I was the one who made magic into the fine art it is today! The aristocrats doffed their hats to ME!

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: So it was jealousy...

dialogues.speaker: Lorenzo
dialogues.text: Jealousy? Hatred, more like. I hated Cesar. All he cared about was his magic — he lived and breathed it.

dialogues.speaker: Lorenzo
dialogues.text: He poured everything into his street performances and his stupid tours like it was just a hobby to him, never bothering to think about Mora. What sort of fool devotes their life to the art of deception and never has a Mora to show for it?

dialogues.speaker: Lorenzo
dialogues.text: But the people loved him, didn't they? Oh, how they looked up to him! No one gave me a second look. All I ever heard was "Oh, your master's amazing, isn't he!"

dialogues.speaker: Lorenzo
dialogues.text: Amazing? Yeah, so amazing that he was completely broke. Every other apprentice was living it up at their master's expense, but no, not me! I put in all the work, mastered all the skills, and it brought me nothing more than the life I already had.

response.speaker: Lorenzo
response.text: He forbade me from using magic to trick people out of their Mora. There was nothing he hated more than that.

response.speaker: Lorenzo
response.text: And with his reputation in Fontaine, it was too risky for me to go it alone. As long as he was alive, if I dabbled in my own brand of money-making magic, he would expose me, and it would destroy me.

response.speaker: Lorenzo
response.text: I had to kill him... There was no other way. He had to go.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: And this was your only motive?

response.speaker: Lorenzo
response.text: It was reason enough. What other motive would I need?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Well, I was under the impression that there might have been other factors at play. For instance... Maybe you were in love with Jemma, but she was engaged to Cesar.

response.speaker: Lorenzo
response.text: In love with Jemma? D—Don't be ridiculous...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Guess I was wrong about that, then. Next question: Are you The Phantom Weasel?

response.speaker: Lorenzo
response.text: ...I am.

response.speaker: Lorenzo
response.text: Cesar was so strict with me. He insisted that his way was the right way. That the sole purpose of magic was to bring joy to the world.

response.speaker: Lorenzo
response.text: I never bought into any of that. I was more interested in the practical value of magic... Sure enough, it helped me fill my pockets with all kinds of valuable treasures.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But I heard that The Phantom Weasel stole from the rich and poor alike.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, yeah. Charlotte told us that The Weasel would steal whatever people valued, no matter how much it was worth.

response.speaker: Lorenzo
response.text: That's just how it looked from the outside. What would any thief want with second-rate loot? I've only ever targeted high-value items.

response.speaker: Lorenzo
response.text: I stole cheap things as a way of practicing my craft. It was other people's overactive imaginations that conjured up the preposterous image they then dubbed the "Phantom Weasel."

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: So that's the story, huh? Well, I hope you're ready to tell it all over again during your trial?

response.speaker: Lorenzo
response.text: What choice do I have? You're a pack of wolves and you've got me between your jaws. You've seen what's here, and my last-ditch effort to stop it getting out has failed. What else can I do?

response.speaker: Lorenzo
response.text: So be it. I've enjoyed power and wealth for the last ten years, the likes of which Cesar could never give me. I wouldn't choose for things to end this way, but I regret nothing.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Very well. In that case, I'll contact the Gardes.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, keep an eye on Lorenzo for me. I'll meet you just outside the workshop when I'm back.

dialogues.speaker: Wishlist
dialogues.text: "I'd like a little dove."

dialogues.speaker: Wishlist
dialogues.text: "I want a robot with cool powers!"

dialogues.speaker: Wishlist
dialogues.text: Note: You need your parents' permission to own a pet, and you also need to take good care of it.

dialogues.speaker: Wishlist
dialogues.text: I've brought a fluffy toy dove for you this time. If you're ready to own a pet, I'll make a real dove appear for you next time. — Cesar

dialogues.speaker: Wishlist
dialogues.text: "I want a bucket of fried chicken that never runs out."

dialogues.speaker: Wishlist
dialogues.text: "I'd like a new bag."

dialogues.speaker: Wishlist
dialogues.text: Note: There is no such thing as fried chicken that never runs out, just as there's no such thing as children who never grow up.

dialogues.speaker: Wishlist
dialogues.text: Also, eating too much fried food is bad for you. Make sure to pair it with something healthy, like a salad, alright? — Cesar

dialogues.speaker: Wishlist
dialogues.text: "I wish my parents would get back together."

dialogues.speaker: Wishlist
dialogues.text: "I wish for good grades in my next exam."

dialogues.speaker: Wishlist
dialogues.text: "I wish for my little sister to have a normal life free of danger."

dialogues.speaker: Wishlist
dialogues.text: Note: I want you to know that you can always share your troubles with me, children. But some wishes need more than magic to make them come true — they need the power of your hard work.

dialogues.speaker: Wishlist
dialogues.text: I wish you the best of luck, and hope that all of your wishes will come true. — Cesar

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: ...Ah. You're back.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: You were so quick. I've only just finished my third dessert.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Your third!? Lynette, come on, we've talked about this, everything in moderation... You're not gonna have any room left for dinner now.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: That's fine. I'll shift to Exercise Mode and jog off the excess sugar.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: That's besides the point... *sigh* Well, it's done now. But try to eat a more balanced diet in the future.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Point taken.

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: Did... everything go okay?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Of course. Lorenzo was no match for us! The Gardes are taking him into custody as we speak.

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: Gosh. That's amazing... I'm sorry, I still didn't know if I could trust you, but now it seems I can.

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: I had my suspicions about Lorenzo, but I... *sob*

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's okay, we understand. He did threaten you. Paimon would find it hard to trust strangers in your position too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But you don't need to be scared anymore. Everything's gonna be okay!

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: Sorry... Sorry, my emotions are all over the place right now. I've been waiting for this day to come for so long.

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: I always wanted to report Lorenzo. He took all of Cesar's property, which I found suspicious, but I had people watching me all the time, so I couldn't risk looking into it...

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: I was so afraid... I was scared he'd do something terrible to me, and then no one would be left to visit Cesar's grave... so I never had the courage to speak out.

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: Thank you all, truly. Thank you so much...

talks.objective: Hand Lorenzo over to the Gardes

dialogues.speaker: Bruno
dialogues.text: Lyney has told me the whole story.

dialogues.speaker: Bruno
dialogues.text: Lorenzo, do you confess to the murder of Cesar, and to framing him for the Phantom Weasel's crimes?

dialogues.speaker: Lori
dialogues.text: Hmph. Look who's finally developed a conscience.

dialogues.speaker: Lori
dialogues.text: What kind of disciple murders their own master? I hope it was worth it, because there'll be hell to pay!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew. Looks like it's all over. What should we do next, Lyney? Should we start preparing for your show?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Let me think...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Let's rendezvous with Lynette and Jemma first. With Lorenzo in custody, Jemma will no longer have to fear for her safety.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Good point! We should go tell Jemma the good news right away. It'll give her some peace of mind for sure!

talks.objective: Explain the situation to Lynette and Jemma
Go to the cemetery to hold a memorial for Cesar

dialogues.speaker: Baltasar
dialogues.text: Thank you all for clearing Cesar's name.

dialogues.speaker: Baltasar
dialogues.text: I never would have guessed that Lorenzo was the real Phantom Weasel... He never showed any signs that there were problems between him and Cesar in public. From the outside, it looked like they got along great.

dialogues.speaker: Baltasar
dialogues.text: Ugh, to think that lowlife's been living life to the fullest all this time while Cesar's name was getting dragged through the mud. It's a travesty...

dialogues.speaker: Baltasar
dialogues.text: At least his soul can finally rest in peace now, thanks to your efforts.

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: If... If only I'd realized before it was too late...

dialogues.speaker: Gracia
dialogues.text: Don't blame yourself, Jemma. This isn't your fault.

dialogues.speaker: Dolora
dialogues.text: Yeah. You still have the rest of your life to live. Cesar wouldn't want to see you spend it feeling guilty.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Cheer up, Jemma.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: My brother's doing a magic show at the opera house tomorrow evening. Would you like to come along? It might raise your spirits.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: This show will be a special one. We're holding it in Cesar's honor.

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: In Cesar's honor? Really?

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: Thank you. I'll be there.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: #Great! We'll see you tomorrow evening. {NICKNAME}, Paimon, don't be late~

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't worry, we'll be there. No way are we gonna miss out on a free magic show!

dialogues.speaker: Juliano
dialogues.text: Jemma's hurt, you say?

dialogues.speaker: Juliano
dialogues.text: Now that you mention it, I did see her getting into a heated argument a while back...

dialogues.speaker: Juliano
dialogues.text: Maybe someone who hates Cesar was taking it out on her... People can be unbelievable sometimes.

dialogues.speaker: Baltasar
dialogues.text: A lot of people find cemeteries bleak and oppressive, but not me.

dialogues.speaker: Baltasar
dialogues.text: I find the silence gives me a sense of peace. And something about being in the presence of the dead and buried... It sorta puts all of life's woes in perspective.

dialogues.speaker: Gracia
dialogues.text: Oh, Cesar... Were you or weren't you The Phantom Weasel?

dialogues.speaker: Lorenzo
dialogues.text: ...At least I can finally stop looking over my shoulder now.

dialogues.speaker: Wishlist
dialogues.text: "When do we get to go to your wedding, Uncle Cesar?"

dialogues.speaker: Wishlist
dialogues.text: "I wanna watch your shows even when I'm grown up, Uncle Cesar!"

dialogues.speaker: Wishlist
dialogues.text: "Do you have to go on tour? Can't you stay here with us, Uncle Cesar?"

dialogues.speaker: Wishlist
dialogues.text: Note: Oh my... This round of wishes has rather exceeded my expectations. The wedding will be held very soon, and don't worry, you're all invited!

dialogues.speaker: Wishlist
dialogues.text: The tour has already been scheduled, but I will definitely be back. And you'll always be welcome at my shows if you like magic. — Cesar

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This book's thick as a brick... Let's take a peek inside it, shall we?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Wishlists...

dialogues.speaker: Cesar's Diary
dialogues.text: At one of my shows a few days ago, a child asked me how I pulled candy out of my hat.

dialogues.speaker: Cesar's Diary
dialogues.text: As a joke, I told the kid that the hat has a built-in wish-granting machine... Next thing I know, today a whole bunch of kids were pestering me to pull all sorts of things out of the hat...

dialogues.speaker: Cesar's Diary
dialogues.text: So I told them another white lie: "The machine needs time to power up, but in the meantime, you can write your wishes down." Well, they took me up on that offer enthusiastically... As I write this, I've only just got back from running around all over town, buying the things they wanted. Boy, are my legs sore...

dialogues.speaker: Cesar's Diary
dialogues.text: I wound up saving very little this month, but that's not a major issue. I now have a bigger problem: How am I going to hide all these things inside my hat...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Children Studying Magic...

dialogues.speaker: Cesar's Diary
dialogues.text: Two children came to talk to me after today's show. I don't know why they were out on their own — they looked much too young to be unsupervised. I do hope they got home safely.

dialogues.speaker: Cesar's Diary
dialogues.text: Anyway, they said that they wanted me to teach them how to do magic. It's not uncommon for children to ask this, of course, but I've never seen any of them as serious about it as these two.

dialogues.speaker: Cesar's Diary
dialogues.text: I told them that learning magic is very hard work, but that didn't faze them at all — it's like they already knew. They seemed so committed... I couldn't turn them down.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Lorenzo's Issues...

dialogues.speaker: Cesar's Diary
dialogues.text: It seems like something's bothering Lorenzo lately, but he won't open up to me about it.

dialogues.speaker: Cesar's Diary
dialogues.text: Surely, he's not upset that I agreed to teach those two children? I'll have to talk him around...

dialogues.speaker: Cesar's Diary
dialogues.text: I have a good feeling about those kids. They're naturally talented, and it seems like they're not new to the world of magic.

dialogues.speaker: Cesar's Diary
dialogues.text: They have all sorts of fantastic ideas. All I'm really doing is helping them develop a more professional-standard training plan.

dialogues.speaker: Cesar's Diary
dialogues.text: They wanted to call me "Master," but I told them they absolutely mustn't. Any magician worth their salt could've taught them what I have... They're the geniuses here. Compared to them, I don't deserve to be called any sort of "master."

dialogues.speaker: Cesar's Diary
dialogues.text: With time, I have no doubt that they could become far greater magicians than I. My only concern is why they're so mature for their age... I fear they've had to grow up too fast. I don't dare to imagine what they must have been through.

dialogues.speaker: Cesar's Diary
dialogues.text: Jemma thinks so too. She doesn't like being around them — says that their eyes are "too piercing." They don't bother me, but then again, I've never been the sharpest tool in the shed.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Farewell...

dialogues.speaker: Cesar's Diary
dialogues.text: It's nearly time for me to go on tour. I asked the two kids if they'd like to come with me, but they shook their heads.

dialogues.speaker: Cesar's Diary
dialogues.text: I once overheard them talking about their "Father" and their "mission"... Sounds like their parents have other plans for them. I guess we'll be parting ways soon.

dialogues.speaker: Cesar's Diary
dialogues.text: It's only been ten days since I first met them, but I think that I've gotten a feel for their personalities now.

dialogues.speaker: Cesar's Diary
dialogues.text: They're very tough, but also very cautious — and they trust no one but each other. This, I fear, is not a good habit to have.

dialogues.speaker: Cesar's Diary
dialogues.text: They hide things from me, too. For example, when I asked them where they live and why they wanted to learn magic, they lied.

dialogues.speaker: Cesar's Diary
dialogues.text: That's the thing about children — whenever they're trying to cover something up, it always shows somehow...

dialogues.speaker: Cesar's Diary
dialogues.text: I can sense that their lives have been hard — possibly even dangerous, too. They're not like other children... It's a shame that I can't do more to help them.

dialogues.speaker: Cesar's Diary
dialogues.text: After thinking things over, I decided to tell them a bit about how I see the world: It's full of lies and falsehoods, and that is why we must find our own truth.

dialogues.speaker: Cesar's Diary
dialogues.text: P.S. I hope they won't find my nagging annoying. Children are so opinionated nowadays. Will it do them more harm than good for someone they've only known ten days to lecture them like that?

dialogues.speaker: Cesar's Diary
dialogues.text: P.P.S. Maybe I'm overthinking this. Children aren't interested in grand philosophies — it probably just went in one ear and out the other. I bet they've already forgotten every word I said.

dialogues.speaker: Cesar's Diary
dialogues.text: Oh, Cesar, Cesar... Just mind your own business next time.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: At Lyney's suggestion, everyone goes to the cemetery to announce Lorenzo's arrest and hold a memorial for Cesar.
